_about: The MCP Events wire format every SDK (pkg/wakeshift, sdk/typescript, sdk/python) serves for chat.message ({channel}), as a client that speaks SEP-3415 sees it: events/list's delivery modes, and for events/subscribe and events/poll, the client's params, what the SDK asks Wakeshift (core_request: the body without call and dialect), what Wakeshift answers (core_response) and the JSON-RPC result the client gets.

subscribe.name: a refresh with a replay bound, and how delivery is going

poll.name: a poll with no cursor at all, as a client may send it
events after a cursor, with more waiting and some skipped

next._comment: Next release: who may subscribe, on the MCP Events wire and through a tool. Loaders that predate it ignore this key. Under the next release, chat.message in subscribe and poll above is defined with public: true (otherwise it's tools-only and those cases are refused); each case above still holds unchanged. Two more events: crawl.finished, tools-only (declares neither personal, authorize nor public), arguments {job: string, required}, payload {pages: number}; deploy.finished, with an authorize that allows only user u1, arguments {env: string, required}, payload {status: string}. user is what identify returns (null: no user). Every refusal is answered by the SDK itself: Wakeshift isn't asked (no request to /events/subscribe or /events/poll), and the error is the dialect's forbidden code, its message from event-tools.json, data null. A draft client is any client name (some-draft-client); chatgpt is ChatGPT's dialect, as in errors.json rpc.
next._c1_dependent: The core refuses the same requests (C1) for events whose manifest says subscribe: "tools", so an old SDK instance can't reopen them; these SDK fixtures check only the SDK's own refusal and that it never asks the core. Without C1 deployed, the SDK's refusal still holds.
next._events_list_comment: events/list names only events a native client may subscribe to; crawl.finished (tools-only) is absent.

tool_subscribe_states._comment: call.subscribe(event, args) from a tool that declares the event, per access and caller: the Subscription's state (and reason), whether the block carries a native line telling the client what to subscribe to, and whether the SDK asks Wakeshift (POST /event-subscriptions). access: tools (crawl.finished-like, no setting), personal, public, authorize_allows / authorize_refuses (deploy.finished, allowing only u1). caller: bridged (Claude Code: recognized as a conversation the SDK subscribes) or native (an MCP Events client that subscribes itself). Arguments: crawl.finished {job: j1}, deploy.finished {env: prod}, a personal event {table: oak}, a public event {channel: eng}. error: call.subscribe throws UsageError with that code. logs: the warnings.json code logged (once per tool and reason). created has id, user, session (redacted when printed) and recognized; native has user and recognized; unavailable has reason; disabled has nothing. On a disabled client every row is state disabled with nothing asked (disabled-client.json).

vouchers._comment: Subscribe vouchers. The events are next's: crawl.finished tools-only, chat.message public, deploy.finished authorize (only u1). feature: whether the core's manifest answer (PUT /manifest, POST /manifest/merge) reports features ["subscribe_vouchers"]; absent means true. A client writes the voucher a tool result handed it as the argument wakeshift_voucher. The SDK takes it out of arguments before anything else reads them (parsing, authorize, onSubscribe, logs, the subscription key) and, for a tools-only event while the feature is on, sends it to Wakeshift as the top-level voucher, skipping the no-user refusal (user null: identify gave none; the core then decides). core_request is the body without call and dialect; call_user is call.user on the wire (null: none sent). An open event ignores a voucher; events/poll of a tools-only event is refused, voucher or not; with the feature off a voucher is never forwarded. on_subscribe: what onSubscribe gets (null: it doesn't run); it runs when Wakeshift answers created with via tool:<name>. core_refused: Wakeshift's answer (status and body) and the JSON-RPC error the client gets. The voucher is a fake.

push._comment: MCP Events push (events/stream), and the push contract. The events are next's: crawl.finished tools-only, chat.message public ({channel}), deploy.finished authorize (only u1). Push is served when the core's manifest answer reports features ["push"], the transport streams its responses (not JSON-response mode) and the app hasn't turned push off; then events/list's delivery is delivery (an open event) or delivery_tools_only (a tools-only event listed with a voucher), and otherwise events/stream answers not_served. streams: a client (draft dialect, user: identify's, null for none) sends params with JSON-RPC id; the SDK asks Wakeshift POST /api/apps/v1/events/stream with core_request (the body without call; call_user is call.user, null for none sent); Wakeshift answers 200 NDJSON with frames, one per line; the client gets notifications (each with _meta io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId: the request's id, string or number, as sent), then result (the final StreamEventsResult, whose _meta carries the subscription ID too). terminated_codes: a terminated frame's error name as the notification's error code, by dialect. refused: answered before any upstream opens, with error (code by dialect; data null: none); core_status and core_error: Wakeshift's refusal of the upstream (no core_status: Wakeshift isn't asked for a stream; HTTP 400 for header, the Mcp-Name header, over HTTP). result instead of error (for the request's id, which the SDK stamps on it as on a stream's result): the client's stream ends with the final result, no notifications: for a 503, after Retry-After (retry_after, seconds, sent as the header; at most 10 s) plus up to 1 s of jitter, so at least retry_after seconds after the request (min_ms), or at once if the client aborts.

reauthorize._comment: While a push stream is open, the SDK asks identify and the event's authorize again every interval (attach's push reauthorizeMs: default_ms by default; a value under min_ms or over max_ms is clamped, clamp[] pins it; invalid[] values are refused as a configuration error). A refusal (authorize false; identify giving no user, or another user, than at open; requireUser refusing) ends that stream as a revocation does: notification (the terminated notification, code by dialect: code), then result, and the upstream is aborted. The core isn't asked to end the subscription: a reconnect asks again and is refused, as at open. identify or authorize throwing or timing out (an error, not a refusal) keeps the stream and logs its category-only code (identify_error, authorize_failed). The stream: deploy.finished {env: prod}, user u1, JSON-RPC id stream_id, authorize allowing u1 at open and refusing at the first check.

core_errors._comment: Wakeshift's refusals of a webhook events/subscribe (chat.message, public; user u1) and the JSON-RPC error each SDK answers, in each dialect (draft: some-draft-client; chatgpt: openai-mcp). Where the callback can't be reached (not https, an address that isn't public, a failed verification), the core adds error.hint (kind callback_unreachable; alternatives: plugin with install, the docs for a client Wakeshift has a plugin for, and poll, with push when Wakeshift serves it, unless the client takes webhooks alone, as ChatGPT, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent do; it may be empty) and says what to do in its message: the SDK passes the message as it is, and the hint as data.hint, beside reason. No hint, no data.hint. The message never asks for a retry.
